note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Liberia: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident's annual taxable income is free to LRD 70,000, then 5% to 200,000, LRD 6,500 plus 15% to 800,000, and LRD 96,500 plus 25% above; there are no local income taxes.

sources.said: Step 1 ​0 to 70,000 ​Nil ​Step 2 ​70,001 to 200,000 ​5% of the excess over LRD 70,000 ​Step 3 ​200,001 to 800,000 LRD ​6,500 + 15% of the excess over LRD 200,000 ​Step 4 ​800,001 and above LRD ​96,500 + 25% of the excess over LRD 800,000​
There are no special local income taxes on individuals in Liberia.

figures.finding: The tax period is the calendar year; returns are due by 31 March of the next year; employees with at least 90% of income from employment are covered by withholding.

sources.said: The taxable period for individuals is the calendar year, unless a taxpayer is authorised to use a different fiscal year. Tax returns PIT returns must be filed by 31 March of the following year.

figures.finding: Social security is 10% of gross income: the employer pays 6% (2% injury, 4% pension) and the employee 4% (pension), remitted monthly to NASSCORP; the self-employed may contribute voluntarily.

sources.said: The social security contribution rate is 10% of gross income. The employer contributes a total of 6%, consisting of 2% for injury scheme and 4% for the pension scheme, while the employee contributes 4% to the pension scheme.
Self-employed individuals may voluntarily contribute to the pension scheme.

figures.finding: Employers withhold payroll tax at the graduated rates and remit it by the 10th of the next month; payments to resident service providers bear 10% withholding, royalties 15%.

sources.said: Resident: Payment of salaries Graduated rates (5%-25%) Rent on residential property 10% Management and consultancy fees 10% Payment for services rendered 10%
This payment must be made on or before the 10th day of the month following the month in which the salary was paid.

figures.finding: A non-resident individual is taxed at a flat 20%; payments for services to a non-resident bear 20% withholding, royalties 15%; finality was not stated in the source read.

sources.said: The non-resident individual tax rate is currently a flat rate of 20% (previously 15%).
Non-resident: Interest 15% Dividends 15% Royalties 15% License fees 15% Gaming winnings 30% Payments on rent 15% Payments for services 20%

figures.finding: Royalties bear 15% withholding for resident and non-resident payees; no special regime for authors was found.

figures.finding: In 2026 goods tax and services tax are each 13% (the December 2025 Code amendment); VAT replaces GST from 1 January 2027 at 15%, with mandatory registration at USD 20,000 of turnover and a registration window July-December 2026.

sources.said: (3) The rate of goods tax is 13 percent of the Section 1004 taxable amount
The rate of services tax is 13 percent of the taxable amount
Currently, the general rate of GST is 13%. VAT system goes live on January 1, 2027, officially replacing the GST regime.
Mandatory registration threshold: US$ 20,000 (or it's equivalent in LRD). The transition registration window: July-December 2026. Rate: VAT standard rate is 15%
The general rate of GST is 12%.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Liberia-source income, including pay for services performed in Liberia, by withholding in place of the income tax, so the withholding is final unless the non-resident elects to file a return (the election binds that year and the next four, and the tax withheld is then a credit); the payer remits within 10 days after the month. The Code as amended to 2020 set 15% on payments for services; the Tax Amendment Act of 2024 raised it to 20%. Royalties bear 15%.

figures.applies: Non-residents receiving Liberia-source payments (ss. 804-806 of the Liberia Revenue Code)

sources.said: Section 804. Imposition of Tax (a) General Rule. A nonresident person is subject to tax on Liberia-source income (deﬁned in Section 805). In lieu of the generally applicable income tax of Part II, The Personal and Business Income Tax, tax is collected by withholding on payments as speciﬁed in Section 806. … (2) derived in respect of the performance of services or employment exercised in Liberia … (e) Payments for Services Rendered. A payor who makes a payment to a nonresident for services rendered is required to withhold tax at the rate of 15 percent of the amount of the payment … (i) Election. A nonresident subject to tax under this section may elect to ﬁle an income tax return … An amount of tax withheld pursuant to Section 806 is creditable against income tax liability
A payor who makes a payment to a nonresident for services rendered is required to withhold tax at the rate of 20 percent of the amount of the payment
